data.detail: ByteDance agreed to acquire Moonton on 22 March 2021 at a valuation of around US$4 billion (Reuters sources; ByteDance matched a competing Tencent bid); Moonton to operate independently under CEO Yuan Jing; covered by Reuters, CNBC (2021-03-23) and Esports Insider (Tom Daniels, 2021-03-22)
data.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonton (refs: Reuters 'ByteDance acquires gaming studio Moonton at around $4 billion valuation'; CNBC Kharpal 2021-03-23) + https://esportsinsider.com/2021/03/bytedance-acquires-mobile-legends-publisher-moonton-at-a-reported-4bn-valuation

data.detail: CONFLICT NOTE (Wikipedia internal): Wikipedia Moonton lead sentence says 'In October 2021, ByteDance acquired Moonton' while the article body and Reuters/CNBC/Esports Insider date the acquisition agreement to 22 March 2021; October 2021 likely reflects deal completion (ContentAsia eNewsletter 18-24 Oct 2021 cited on Wikipedia) - both dates recorded
27 November 2025: Bloomberg reported ByteDance revived the Moonton sale and was in talks with Savvy Games Group (owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund)
data.source: https://news.google.com/rss/search?q=ByteDance+Moonton+sale (headline: 'ByteDance Is Said to Revive Moonton Sale in Talks With PIF's Savvy Games - Bloomberg.com' seen 2026-10-22)

data.detail: 13 February 2026: Reuters exclusive - ByteDance in talks to sell gaming unit Moonton for more than US$6 billion, sources say; deal could be signed that quarter with key terms agreed
